stem: Which drug-status and Massachusetts legal-consequence pairings are accurate? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Pregabalin is Schedule V, and covered dispensing is MassPAT-reportable.
Gabapentin is federally noncontrolled but Massachusetts Schedule VI and MassPAT-reportable.
Methylphenidate is Schedule II and may not be refilled.
Pseudoephedrine is Schedule V because CMEA restricts retail sales.

explanation.core_reasoning: Drug classification and legal consequence must be matched separately. Pregabalin is Schedule V, gabapentin has a Massachusetts-specific Schedule VI and reporting consequence, and methylphenidate is Schedule II; CMEA controls do not make pseudoephedrine Schedule V.

choice_analysis.A: Pregabalin is federally and in Massachusetts Schedule V, and covered dispensing belongs in MassPAT reporting.
choice_analysis.B: Gabapentin is not federally scheduled but Massachusetts treats it as Schedule VI and an additional MassPAT-reportable drug.
choice_analysis.C: Methylphenidate is a Schedule II stimulant, so a prescription may not be refilled.
choice_analysis.D: Pseudoephedrine has federal retail controls as a listed chemical product, but those controls do not create Schedule V status.

related_facts: Reporting status does not change federal schedule.
A therapeutic class is not a legal schedule.
explanation.mpje_trap: Converting every monitored or restricted product into a federally scheduled drug.

reasoning_steps: Separate CMEA controls from CSA scheduling
